name: Mount Eden / Johnson Landing salt works (SR-92 to Hayward Landing)
note: John Johnson leveed 14 acres of naturally saline marsh at Mt Eden in 1853 (first harvest 25 t, shipped by schooner), just north of today's SR-92 - the first solar salt works on the Bay (EDAW 2005 after Sandoval 1988); the natural salinas here are on the 1857 Coast Survey T-sheet (SFEI) and USFWS's 'natural salt ponds c.1850'. Small family works (American Salt Co., Marsicano family, from the early 1860s) followed. Ponds and crystallizers still drawn at Johnson Landing on the 1942 Hayward sheet (1939 photos). Works on ground that is marsh or fill today end c.1955 (LOW).

name: Lake Merced

note: 'Created in 1964 when the Alameda Flood Control and Water Conservation District dammed San Lorenzo Creek' (East Bay Regional Park District). Before: valley floor / creek.

name: Lake Anza (Tilden Park)
note: 'Created by the construction of the C L Tilden Park Dam in 1938' on Wildcat Creek, financed by the Public Works Administration. Before: valley floor / creek.

name: Upper San Leandro Reservoir (arm outside the main ring)
note: Arm of Upper San Leandro Reservoir that the ring of lake_upper_san_leandro_reservoir does not reach (it fell to the post-war default); same dam year 1926.

name: Bear Gulch Reservoir
note: Bear Gulch Dam (California Water Service Company, Bear Gulch District; Atherton / Woodside), completed 1896. Before: valley floor / creek (the dam year is when water first stood here).

name: Cherry Flat Reservoir
note: Cherry Flat Dam on Upper Penitencia Creek above Alum Rock Park (City of San Jose), completed 1936 per the National Inventory of Dams (CA00158). Before: valley floor / creek (the dam year is when water first stood here).

name: Lake Ranch Reservoir
note: Lake Ranch Reservoir above Saratoga (San Jose Water Company: 'the oldest dam in our system'), two earth dams; completed 1877 per the National Inventory of Dams (CA00676). Before: valley floor / creek (the dam year is when water first stood here).

name: Sandy Wool Lake
note: Ed R. Levin County Park's dam (County of Santa Clara, earth, 38 ft) completed 1968 per the National Inventory of Dams (CA00890, listed under the park's name); taken as Sandy Wool Lake's dam, the park's only large one. Before: valley floor / creek (the dam year is when water first stood here).

name: Lake Lucerne
note: Lake Lucerne at Bean Hollow south of Pescadero: earth dam 'Bean Hollow #2' of the Lake Lucerne Mutual Water Company, completed 1938 per the National Inventory of Dams. Before: valley floor / creek (the dam year is when water first stood here).
